newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin moves to complete recovery near forest.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin moves to complete recovery near forest.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin moved on Monday to his Rus country residence west of Moscow for the "final stage" of his rehabilitation after heart bypass surgery, the Kremlin said.

Yeltsin's press office said the Rus, 100 km (60 miles) from Moscow, had better facilities for 65-year-old president's outdoor recreation than the Gorky-9 residence just outside the capital where he had moved last week.
"It has conditions allowing both the finalising of rehabilitation and work and active recreation," a brief press office statement said.
Interfax news agency said Yeltsin, who underwent a quintuple bypass surgery on November 5, had been flown from Gorky-9 to Rus on helicopter.
"Apart from routine work the president ... is expected to make walks in the picturesque forests surrounding the residence," Interfax said.
Rus, earlier known as Zavidovo, has been a favourite hunting site for Soviet leaders, who had often invited foreign dignitaries to shoot wild boars or ducks there.
It was not clear whether Yeltsin, also a devoted hunter, would be allowed to hunt.
Doctors have complained that a visit to Rus before the operation worsened the president's heart condition and made things more difficult for those who prepared him for surgery.

Kremlin doctors say Yeltsin is now recovering well, however. The head of parliament's upper house, Yegor Stroyev, who visited Yeltsin last week, said the president could make a trial visit to his Kremlin office by December 25.
The Kremlin has said Yeltsin will meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, expected in Moscow on January 4, at Rus.

Yeltsin has also invited French President Jacques Chirac to visit him in early January. The meeting has so far been arranged in principle, but there have been no reports whether it would take place at Rus or in the Kremlin.
Yeltsin is also planning to visit the United States in the first half of 1997.
